limitations_and_construct_boundary: 直接题目相关，但主要为规范性框架和通用XAI方法描述，不能作为图像鉴伪解释可靠性的实证依据。所述图像/视频SHAP/LIME用法也未做验证。
screening_conclusion: 纳入相关工作地图的概念性邻接；不纳入经验性可靠性证据。

paper: Explain To Me: Salience-Based Explainability for Synthetic Face Detection Models
verified_identity: Colton R. Crum et al.; IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence 5(6), 2766–2778 (2024); DOI 10.1109/TAI.2023.3333310; arXiv:2303.11969v2 (submitted 2023-03-21, revised 2023-03-27)
relevance_class: 强相关邻接：synthetic-face detection的定量saliency/XAI行为评价；非局部操纵取证
scope_and_methods: arXiv官方HTML全文核读。使用10,000张FFHQ真脸和四种StyleGAN生成脸；评价子集为4,000真/4,000假。DenseNet121、ResNet50的Grad-CAM，对照交叉熵与CYBORG人类显著性监督训练。定义五类汇总指标：S_entropy、S_noise（盐椒噪声下SSIM）、S_resilience（平移/翻转/90度旋转并逆变换对齐）、S_focus（模糊显著区与非显著区后看AUROC和热图变化）、S_stability（每个架构/训练配置十个独立seed的热图SSIM）。
observed_reliability_evidence: 实证报告不同模型/训练方案在显著图集中度、输入噪声反应、几何变换跟随、显著/背景模糊反应和跨seed稳定性上的差异；人类显著性监督模型总体表现出更高跨seed一致性。作者把这些定位为可扩展的模型行为解释指标。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 任务是整脸合成/真实分类，不是局部篡改定位或拼接检测。CYBORG的人类标注参与训练监督；本文没有独立用户评价，也未以独立篡改区域真值验证解释正确性。S_focus以模型自身显著图选区并再看模型性能/新显著图变化，存在自参照性；熵/稳定/几何一致性是行为质量代理，不等同因果忠实或足够法证证据。噪声/变换类型由作者说明为示例，需按任务适配。
screening_conclusion: 纳入图像真实性XAI量化评价的重要前史/强方法邻接。对本题可迁移的是稳定性、输入扰动和受控删除测试设计；不能把其人类引导训练或高saliency稳定性误写为用户信任校准或局部篡改证据真值。

paper: Quantitative Analysis of Visual XAI for Multiclass DeepFake Detection Based on CNN
verified_identity: Leandro Santiago de Araújo et al.; 2025 38th SIBGRAPI Conference on Graphics, Patterns and Images; IEEE DOI 10.1109/SIBGRAPI67909.2025.11223365; conference 30 Sep–3 Oct 2025
relevance_class: 核心直接候选；原文证据部分核对，完整PDF不可得
scope_and_methods: IEEE Xplore官方摘要及References [1]-[23]已直接核对；官方会议PDF索引片段包含AOS定义及实验表。FaceForensics++多类面部操纵；比较ResNet50、EfficientNetB7、InceptionV3、ConvNeXt上的Grad-CAM、SmoothGrad、Integrated Gradients、Input×Gradient、Saliency；报告显著图熵、噪声响应、几何变换resilience、SLIC segmentation AOS，并将指标输入Random Forest区分类别。完整PDF端点访问超时，因此操作细节仍是部分核对。
observed_reliability_evidence: 官方索引正文显示AOS把最显著区删除后量化预测改变；Table I的检测准确率约91%–94%，Tables III–IV给不同解释器统计量及基于这些量的RF分类率。这些证明作者提出了定量行为/判别代理，不代表解释已通过独立法证证据验证。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 作者将AOS解释为functional sufficiency，但实际删除已高亮特征后测输出下降，构念更接近necessity/comprehensiveness或deletion sensitivity；经典sufficiency应检验仅保留被解释特征时能否维持输出。当前可访问原文内容未显示独立伪造区域mask/专家真值或人类适当依赖评估；仅有预测准确率不能验证解释正确性。已读的是官方摘要、引用列表与索引正文片段，不能声称已取得完整PDF/阅读全文。IEEE Xplore显示[1]-[23]共23个编号；ResearchGate元数据显示References 25，主来源计数差异保留。
screening_conclusion: 高优先级直接候选；论文真正贡献是鉴伪场景下视觉XAI指标的应用和比较。采用时必须区分稳定性/扰动敏感/模型预测差异与grounded causal faithfulness，且将AOS操作化作为待检验构念问题。完整全文核查仍待出版社PDF可访问。

paper: MENTOR: Human Perception-Guided Pretraining for Increased Generalization
verified_identity: Colton R. Crum and Adam Czajka; arXiv:2310.19545 (submitted 2023-10-30; v3 2025-04-26)
relevance_class: 强方法邻接：synthetic-face detection人工saliency预训练和CAM熵分析；非直接局部取证faithfulness验证
scope_and_methods: 全文核读。两阶段MENTOR先以autoencoder在无类别标签下预测人工显著图，再移除decoder并微调分类器；任务为iris PAD、synthetic-face detection和chest X-ray；10个随机seed测AUROC。Face任务使用363名Amazon Mechanical Turk参与者提供的real/fake判断及支持区域标注；训练样本765张（379 real/386 fake），20,000张验证样本。对比Cross-entropy、CYBORG、UNET+Gaze及不同backbone。
observed_reliability_evidence: 作者报告预测CAM的定性图例与test CAM salience entropy；将entropy作为显著图紧致/聚焦的粗代理，并把分析定位为synthetic-face explainability toolkit的一部分。其主实验展示saliency-guided pretraining与分类泛化，不是test explanation的独立真值判定。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: §6.2说明因时间限制仅计算S_entropy；作者承认已使用所有可用human saliency作训练，缺少额外数据以测model saliency与human saliency的效能差异。Entropy只量化紧致性，不能检验解释对模型决策的因果忠实性/局部篡改mask正确性；无用户解释效用或适当依赖实验。Face训练/验证规模及GAN数据域也限制外推。
screening_conclusion: 强方法邻接，纳入2023起synthetic-face explainability研究脉络。重要的是它明确显示‘saliency训练泛化’与‘saliency解释是否正确’是不同终点；保留作者的entropy代理并标明缺少独立human-ground-truth校验。

paper: Grains of Saliency: Optimizing Saliency-based Training of Biometric Attack Detection Models
verified_identity: Colton R. Crum, Samuel Webster, Adam Czajka; IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB), 2024; arXiv:2405.00650
relevance_class: 强方法邻接：synthetic-face detection人类显著图训练与开集泛化；不是解释输出评价
scope_and_methods: 全文核读。研究iris PAD与合成脸检测；比较人工subjects、模仿人类显著性的autoencoder、领域分割模型，以及Boundary/Area/Features of Interest三档salience granularity；ResNet50、DenseNet121、Inception-V3；iris测试AUC跨3次、合成脸跨5次独立训练。合成脸测试集7,000张（1,000 real、6,000 StyleGAN系列合成脸）。
observed_reliability_evidence: 测量saliency来源与粒度对开集检测泛化的效应。synthetic-face结果显示不同架构的最优粒度不同、方差偏宽；这提示人类saliency监督在伪造检测中的效益并不稳定。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 所有主要结果是分类AUROC，不是模型解释与测试图像独立ground truth的对齐、必要/充分证据或模型参数随机化测试；human saliency被用作训练引导而非独立评价基准。只覆盖合成脸与生物PAD，不代表局部图像拼接/修补。
screening_conclusion: 强方法邻接；能支持人类显著监督、标签粒度、架构和跨训练seed的对比设计，不可将分类提升写作解释faithfulness或取证正确性。

paper: SAGE: Saliency-Guided Contrastive Embeddings
verified_identity: Colton R. Crum, Christopher Sweet, Adam Czajka; arXiv:2511.12744v2 (submitted 2025-11-16; revised 2025-12-05)
relevance_class: 强方法邻接：synthetic-face detection上的显著图引导训练与反转图sanity check
scope_and_methods: 全文核读。SAGE以saliency-preserving/degrading模糊增强、logit分布对齐和embedding triplet loss结合人类显著图；任务包含iris PAD、chest X-ray异常与synthetic-face detection；比较CYBORG、UNet+Gaze、Gaze-GNN、MENTOR等；5次独立训练，报告AUROC。附saliency-map反转sanity check。
observed_reliability_evidence: Synthetic-face ResNet50 AUROC：SAGE 0.587±0.060；将人类saliency map反转后0.577±0.037（差0.010）。该干预能有限检查训练收益是否对指定saliency输入敏感；其他任务的差异更大，任务效应不一致。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 研究目标是saliency-guided training的性能/机制，不是解释质量benchmark。合成脸结果较低且反转差异小，不能证明解释是正确/忠实；无真实篡改区域mask、独立证据真值、删除插入评测或用户适当依赖研究。作者把人工标注质量作为留待未来工作的问题。
screening_conclusion: 纳入合成脸解释脉络中少见的saliency反转sanity-check方法；审慎视为低幅度机制证据，不能等同完整faithfulness验证。

paper: Human-Aided Saliency Maps Improve Generalization of Deep Learning
verified_identity: Aidan Boyd, Kevin W. Bowyer, Adam Czajka; IEEE/CVF WACV 2022; arXiv:2105.03492; DOI 10.1109/WACV51458.2022.00132
relevance_class: synthetic/biometric spoof-detection method neighbor: human-saliency training; not explanation-validity evidence
scope_and_methods: Official WACV paper and arXiv abstract reviewed. Human annotations of salient iris PAD image regions are encoded through multilevel blur in a training-data transformation; compare against ordinary augmentation and a larger-data baseline, including leave-one-attack-type-out generalization.
observed_reliability_evidence: Reports lower LivDet-Iris 2020 winner error (29.78% to 16.37%) and improved generalization under unseen attack types. This is detector performance evidence, not an evaluation of post-hoc detector explanations.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: No image-manipulation authenticity task, explanation map ground truth, parameter randomization, deletion/insertion faithfulness, or human reliance endpoint. Human salience is training supervision.
screening_conclusion: Retain as early methodological context for human-derived region supervision; do not count as direct image-forensics XAI reliability evidence.

paper: Human Saliency-Driven Patch-Based Matching for Interpretable Post-Mortem Iris Recognition
verified_identity: Aidan Boyd, Daniel Moreira, Andrey Kuehlkamp, Kevin W. Bowyer, Adam Czajka; WACV Workshops 2023; DOI 10.1109/WACVW58289.2023.00077; arXiv:2208.03138
relevance_class: cross-domain forensic biometrics neighbor: localized evidence display and human evaluation
scope_and_methods: Official CVF WACV workshop full paper reviewed. Patch-Based Matching localizes usable iris texture in post-mortem images and displays corresponding matched regions. The paper includes two human annotation/comparison rounds (152 annotators in step 1; 131 in step 2) and reports human match/non-match accuracy as a design/evaluation comparator.
observed_reliability_evidence: The proposed output exposes local regions supporting match/non-match decisions; the authors explicitly design for human examiner understandability. Human study provides task-level performance evidence for forensic iris matching and visual annotation.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The decision is identity match between iris samples, not whether an image is manipulated/authentic. Region localization is a purpose-built matcher output, not post-hoc attribution faithfulness. Human comparison accuracy does not assess whether users appropriately rely on an XAI system.
screening_conclusion: Include as forensic-explanation and human-evaluation analogy, clearly separated from image forgery authenticity and post-hoc explanation validity.

paper: CYBORG: Blending Human Saliency Into the Loss Improves Deep Learning-Based Synthetic Face Detection
verified_identity: Aidan Boyd, Patrick Tinsley, Kevin W. Bowyer, Adam Czajka; IEEE/CVF WACV 2023; DOI 10.1109/WACV56688.2023.00605; arXiv:2112.00686; official CVF pages 6108–6117 (some early records say 6097–6106)
relevance_class: strong synthetic-face method neighbor: human saliency/CAM alignment in training
scope_and_methods: Official CVF page and PDF reviewed. 363 participants annotated salient regions while judging authentic versus synthetic faces; CAM is compared to human saliency in a training loss. Evaluation tests unseen GAN generators and multiple CNN architectures.
observed_reliability_evidence: Provides human-authored authenticity-region annotations and tests whether supervision improves open-set synthetic-face classification. It therefore offers a useful human-evidence source and a training alignment protocol.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Human annotations supervise training and are not an untouched test set for explanation validity. Reported gains are classification/generalization; no explanation sufficiency/necessity, model randomization, independent causal ground truth or appropriate-reliance study. Scope is fully synthetic face detection rather than local edits.
screening_conclusion: Strong method neighbor to synthetic-image authenticity explanation studies; not direct proof that generated explanations are faithful. Official CVF bibliographic pagination differs from some arXiv/reference-list metadata; canonical identity follows DOI/CVF.

paper: Teaching AI to Teach: Leveraging Limited Human Salience Data Into Unlimited Saliency-Based Training
verified_identity: Colton R. Crum, Aidan Boyd, Kevin Bowyer, Adam Czajka; BMVC 2023 (official proceedings), arXiv:2306.05527
relevance_class: strong synthetic-face/iris saliency training neighbor
scope_and_methods: Official BMVC 2023 page and full-paper content reviewed. Teacher models trained on limited human-saliency annotations produce CAM/RISE maps for larger student training sets; tasks include synthetic-face detection and fake-iris/PAD, evaluated across four CNN architectures.
observed_reliability_evidence: Shows student performance can improve when saliency generated from a human-guided teacher is used; the paper also discusses that a high-scoring teacher can attend to spurious image regions.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Main endpoint is classification AUROC/generalization. No independent test-time explanation ground truth, deletion/insertion, parameter randomization, adversarial explanation robustness or user reliance endpoint. A teacher’s saliency is pseudo-label supervision, not explanation truth.
screening_conclusion: Include as an important synthetic-face XAI-training lineage paper; no direct image-forgery explanation reliability evidence.

paper: Model Focus Improves Performance of Deep Learning-Based Synthetic Face Detectors
verified_identity: Jacob C. Piland, Adam Czajka, Christopher Sweet; IEEE Access 11:63430–63441 (2023); DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3282927; arXiv:2303.00818
relevance_class: strong synthetic-face explanation proxy/entropy-method neighbor
scope_and_methods: Official arXiv HTML full text and IEEE DOI metadata reviewed. Proposes human-saliency-entropy-based, forced-minimum-entropy, DROID log-entropy, and combined CYBORG+DROID training losses; evaluates synthetic-face detection on unseen GANs.
observed_reliability_evidence: CAM entropy is used as a model-focus proxy. Results show lower entropy is associated with performance gains over part of the tested range, but the highest AUROC generally occurs around entropy 2.0–2.5 rather than at the minimum; blending human saliency and DROID slightly raises mean AUROC.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Entropy quantifies concentration, not relevance, causal faithfulness or evidence correctness. This is a training/performance study and does not validate post-hoc maps against independent authenticity annotations or test user reliance.
screening_conclusion: Important precursor to MENTOR/Grains/SAGE and to entropy-based saliency analysis; treat entropy as a proxy with a non-monotonic performance relationship, never as standalone reliability evidence.

paper: DiffGradCAM: A Class Activation Map Using the Full Model Decision to Solve Unaddressed Adversarial Attacks
verified_identity: Jacob Piland, Christopher Sweet, Adam Czajka; CVPR 2026 Findings; arXiv:2506.08514v4 (2026-04-09)
relevance_class: strong XAI reliability-method neighbor: adversarial robustness of CAM explanations
scope_and_methods: Official arXiv v4 full text and version metadata reviewed; CVPR 2026 Findings version identity confirmed. Proposes contrastive DiffGradCAM/++ using the target-vs-competitor logit difference and SHAMs, an entropy-aware passive-fooling benchmark. Experiments cover seven-class iris PAD (five DenseNet runs, human-salience vs SHAM supervision) and ImageNet (5,000 images, four CNN backbones); CAM susceptibility is normalized-map pixel MSE between clean and SHAM-fine-tuned models.
observed_reliability_evidence: On Iris PAD, SHAM-trained AUROC (0.9766±0.0018) is not lower than human-salience-trained AUROC (0.9723±0.0021), while GradCAM is qualitatively redirected. On ImageNet, mean-aggregated DiffGradCAM variants closely match standard maps in clean settings (MSE <1e-3); SHAM susceptibility is generally reduced but varies by architecture and CAM order, with other methods best/tied in some cases.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Map-MSE to GradCAM measures similarity to a baseline, not independent explanation truth; clean-vs-attacked map MSE measures resistance to this specified SHAM manipulation, not causal faithfulness or forensic localization. Insertion/deletion is explicitly judged unsuitable for this passive-fooling threat only. Authors state human studies would further validate utility; no user evaluation or appropriate-reliance outcome is reported. Iris PAD is a biometric presentation-attack task, not digital image manipulation detection.

paper: Do feature attribution methods correctly attribute features?

relevance_class: Strong image-domain controlled-ground-truth method neighbor: compares saliency maps with known localized perturbation regions.; Official Springer metadata and full arXiv text reviewed

screening_conclusion: Useful region-recovery benchmark design; external validity to natural image manipulation remains untested.

paper: Reliable local explanations for machine listening

paper: Post-Hoc Explainable Semantic Image Segmentation: Applications for Interpretability and Adversarial Attacks

paper: Robustness and Explainability in Automatic Speech Recognition and Speaker Verification
verified_identity: Xiaoliang Wu; PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh (2025)
relevance_class: High-value cross-modal reliability neighbor: validates local explanations against manually aligned temporal ground truth and exposes metric/threshold dependence.; Full doctoral thesis reviewed

observed_reliability_evidence: LIME-TS matched the phoneme-level ground-truth segment within its top three explanation segments in 96% of tested cases, outperforming base LIME by up to 44.8% and LIME-WS by up to 17% on all speakers. limitations_and_construct_boundary: High-value cross-modal explanation-validity study, but audio/speech only. The phoneme task has unusually fine-grained ground truth; the reported results do not establish visual-image or forensic validity. screening_conclusion: Strong audio-domain method evidence; no direct visual-forensics result.

paper: Evaluation of Feature Attribution Methods in Interpretable Machine Learning
verified_identity: Paige Rattenberry; BASc Honours Thesis, Simon Fraser University (2022)

It is methodologically closely related to Zhou et al.'s controlled dataset-modification approach and cites that work; treat as an application/extension line rather than independent broad replication. The test is an artificial watermark shortcut in chest X-rays, not natural image forgery or authenticity detection.
screening_conclusion: Useful direct image-region grounding method; external validity to natural forensic edits remains untested.

verified_identity: Limai Jiang et al. (9 authors); arXiv:2602.20511v2 (2026); Springer chapter DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-37664-0_25 also listed by Scholar
relevance_class: Image-domain causal-faithfulness method neighbor: uses controlled patch interventions for segmentation explanations; no forensic task.; Full arXiv HTML reviewed; Springer chapter record identified
scope_and_methods: Introduces perturbation-driven causal reasoning (PdCR), using average treatment effects over image-patch interventions to attribute effects on a target segmentation region; compares against SEG-GRAD and MiSuRe on HAM10000 skin-lesion and FIVES retinal-vessel segmentation.
observed_reliability_evidence: The authors report higher attribution scores than the two baselines across the tested models/datasets and reveal model-dependent segmentation strategies. The experiments use 50 resampled interventions after coarse-to-fine screening; claimed faithfulness remains tied to the selected perturbation distribution, target RoI, Dice-based outcome, and two medical datasets.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Causal image-segmentation explanation method neighbor, not manipulation detection, authenticity, or forensic localization. It is recent; generalization beyond its two medical tasks and intervention construction is unestablished.
screening_conclusion: Useful emerging causal-evaluation design; do not treat its medical segmentation results as proof of forensic explanation validity.

paper: Vliv vizualizací neuronových sítí na rozhodování uživatelů při detekci deepfake pomocí heatmap
verified_identity: Filip Brna; Master's thesis, Brno University of Technology, Faculty of Information Technology, 2025; official PDF, 98 pages
relevance_class: 强相关人类决策/AI依赖邻接证据；不是内禀解释忠实度验证
scope_and_methods: Randomized three-group online study: control, detector score, detector score plus Grad-CAM++ heatmap. The paper reports 204 valid participants (70/67/67); 167 contributed to confidence-weighted-score analyses after excluding records with at least 20% missing confidence responses (56/58/53). Participants judged 60 selected FaceForensics++ images (30 genuine, 30 deepfake); the set was designed to span detector-score bins and include a 50% detector error rate. EfficientNet-B3/B4 detectors were used. Participants gave binary decisions and 5-point confidence ratings; outcomes include accuracy, F1, a custom confidence-weighted score (CWS), agreement/correct override, and post-study self-reported reliance/usefulness. Targeted review of methods, results, feedback and discussion; not cover-to-cover.
observed_reliability_evidence: Overall group differences in accuracy and F1 were not significant (reported Kruskal-Wallis p=.294 and p=.257). Among AI-mispredicted images, median accuracy was 60% control, 52% score-only, and 57% score+heatmap; the omnibus test was significant (H=12.768, p=.0017), but the score-only vs heatmap post-hoc comparison was not (p=.170). For CWS on AI-mispredicted images, a repeated-measures test was significant (p=.0009); Holm-adjusted post-hoc comparison found score-only worse than score+heatmap (p=.048), with medians -.031 and .048 respectively. The correct-override-rate difference itself was not significant (p=.187). In post-study self-report, the heatmap group reported greater reliance on the AI detector than score-only (Mann-Whitney U=1803, p=.0499), while heatmaps were commonly rated only slightly helpful.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: This is direct evidence about human decision behavior and reliance when shown a deepfake detector score plus one visualization, not a test of intrinsic explanation truth or causal faithfulness. It reports no independent artifact/region ground-truth comparison, parameter-randomization test, deletion/insertion test, or counterfactual validation of Grad-CAM++ maps. The participant sample was demographically imbalanced (predominantly young, male, technically educated); the study was an online questionnaire; it used only FaceForensics++ and Grad-CAM++; and the authors note its 60-image, uniformly distributed-score, 50%-AI-error design may not match real-world detector performance. A self-reported reliance item is not equivalent to trial-level appropriate-reliance calibration.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a high-priority human-factors/reliance study directly adjacent to explanation reliability. The evidence is mixed: heatmaps mitigate some confidence-weighted harms on deliberately erroneous detector cases, yet score+heatmap users report higher reliance; the raw-accuracy score-only vs heatmap contrast and correct-override contrast are not statistically significant. Do not cite this thesis as validation that Grad-CAM++ explanations identify true forgery evidence.

paper: AOT-PixelNet: Lightweight and interpretable detection of forged images via adaptive orthogonal transform
verified_identity: Dengtai Tan, Deyi Yang, Boao Tan, Chengyu Niu, Yang Yang, Shichao Li; Applied Soft Computing 185, Part A (2025), article 113873; DOI 10.1016/j.asoc.2025.113873
relevance_class: Adjacent interpretable generated-image authenticity detector; publisher abstract/indexed excerpts reviewed, not full text
scope_and_methods: The publisher abstract describes AOT-PixelNet: an Adaptive Orthogonal Transform front end (FFT/DCT and other orthogonal transforms) plus a lightweight 1×1-convolution PixelNet for AI-generated image detection. It reports cross-generator experiments and Grad-CAM visual analysis; the abstract says the maps focus on background regions of generated images. Review limited to publisher abstract and indexed introduction/contribution excerpts because the full ScienceDirect page returned 403.
observed_reliability_evidence: The paper presents frequency-transform differences and Grad-CAM visualizations as interpretability evidence. The available material does not show an independent forged-region ground truth, deletion/insertion or counterfactual faithfulness test, explanation sanity check, human validation, or appropriate-reliance experiment.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: This is AI-generated-image detection with an interpretable detector design, not a direct image-tampering explanation-reliability study. Background-focused Grad-CAM patterns and cross-generator classification performance do not establish explanation truth or causal dependence. Full methods/results/limitations were not accessible; do not infer absent tests from abstract-only materials.
screening_conclusion: Retain as an adjacent candidate because it combines image authenticity detection and visual interpretability. Keep it below direct explanation-reliability evaluation studies until full text is available; do not cite current evidence as a faithfulness validation.

paper: Explainable AI-Generated Image Forensics: A Low-Resolution Perspective with Novel Artifact Taxonomy
verified_identity: Kaustubh Sharma; Explainable AI-Generated Image Forensics: A Low-Resolution Perspective with Novel Artifact Taxonomy; IEEE/CVF ICCV Workshops 2025, APAI workshop, pp. 1587–1596; official CVF paper.
relevance_class: Direct image-forensics explanation method; reliability validity not established in the reviewed paper.
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the complete 10-page official CVF workshop paper (body pp.1–8, references pp.9–10). The method detects AI-generated images at 32×32 resolution and uses an artifact taxonomy plus SinSR, CLIP-guided artifact selection, and a VLM to produce textual/visual explanations. The detector reports 98.65% accuracy, 13.4 ms inference, and 96.80% under its adversarial setup.
observed_reliability_evidence: The article states an artifact-annotated explanation benchmark was unavailable, so it reports qualitative examples/visual inspection rather than quantitative explanation correctness or localization agreement. No independent explanation ground truth, human explanation-quality study, inter-rater agreement, parameter-randomization sanity test, deletion/insertion, causal sufficiency/necessity, or appropriate-reliance experiment was found in the full paper.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: High detector accuracy and visually plausible artifact descriptions do not establish that the explanation is factually grounded in the actual synthetic evidence or causally faithful to the detector. The result is a workshop paper and the explanation-validity evidence is qualitative only.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a direct task/method candidate and high-priority full-text review, but do not cite as demonstrating reliable explanations. The reference audit is separately recorded as 47 numbered positions; most cited papers were screened by citation metadata, not read in full.

paper: SynArtifact: Classifying and Alleviating Artifacts in Synthetic Images via Vision-Language Model
verified_identity: Bin Cao, Jianhao Yuan, Yexin Liu, Jian Li, Shuyang Sun, Jing Liu, Bo Zhao; arXiv:2402.18068v3, 2024 (version posted 2024-11-18).
relevance_class: Method adjacency: synthetic-image artifact classification and box grounding, not forensic authenticity explanation evaluation.
scope_and_methods: Read the official arXiv v3 HTML. SynArtifact-1K contains 1,310 text-image examples (768 with artifacts, 542 without); human annotations provide artifact class, caption, and coordinates. The paper reports 13 artifact types and evaluates a fine-tuned VLM on a 1,045/265 train/test split. It computes IoU against human boxes for artifact localization.
observed_reliability_evidence: The VLM reaches 45.66% artifact-classification accuracy and 52.02 F1; distortion F1 is 52.23. For localization, the authors report that predictions often use oversized boxes containing multiple artifacts and say precise localization is difficult. The n=18, 1–7 user study rates image quality after artifact alleviation, not explanation correctness or detector explanations.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: This is a useful artifact-grounding/evaluation design neighbor because it uses human boxes and IoU, but the object is synthetic-image quality rather than authentic-versus-forged classification. The reported user study does not validate explanations; no forensic explanation faithfulness or appropriate reliance is tested. The paper does not report annotator agreement in the reviewed body.
screening_conclusion: Include as a method-adjacent source for box-grounded artifact assessment and its localization failure modes; do not classify as a direct image-forgery XAI reliability study.

paper: AEROBLADE: Training-Free Detection of Latent Diffusion Images Using Autoencoder Reconstruction Error
verified_identity: Jonas Ricker, Denis Lukovnikov, Asja Fischer; AEROBLADE: Training-Free Detection of Latent Diffusion Images Using Autoencoder Reconstruction Error; CVPR 2024; arXiv:2401.17879v2.
relevance_class: Method adjacency: image-forensic reconstruction-error maps and inpainting localization.
scope_and_methods: Read the official arXiv v2 HTML, including methodology, detection experiments, qualitative inpainting analysis, perturbation tests, discussion, and references. AEROBLADE uses latent-diffusion autoencoder reconstruction error (including LPIPS maps) to distinguish generated from real images and inspect local reconstruction anomalies; reported mean AP is 0.992 across evaluated generators.
observed_reliability_evidence: The paper visually shows lower reconstruction error in Stable-Diffusion-inpainted regions of real images. Its text explicitly states that predicting precise inpainted-region locations is future work; no quantitative region overlap/recall or independent explanation-correctness evaluation is reported for these maps.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: This is a forensic evidence-map method, not a conventional post-hoc explanation test. Detection AP and input-corruption robustness do not establish that a local map is a faithful explanation; the inpainting localization evidence is qualitative and not evaluated against independent ground-truth masks.
screening_conclusion: Add as a useful neighboring forensic localization paper. The malformed CVF reference [18] is not reliable bibliographic metadata for this work; retain both the error and the corrected official identity in the ledger.

paper: Text Over Image: Auditing Multimodal Robustness in Synthetic Medical Image Detection
verified_identity: Ching-Hao Chiu, Hao-Wei Chung, Gelei Xu, Xueyang Li, Pin-Yu Chen, John Kheir, Meysam Ghaffari, Carlos Morato, Ahmed Abbasi, Yiyu Shi; arXiv:2606.25375v2, posted 2026-07-01; extended MICCAI 2026 work titled Beyond Visual Forensics: Auditing Multimodal Robustness for Synthetic Medical Image Detection.
relevance_class: Deployment/reliance robustness adjacency for synthetic medical-image authenticity decisions; not visual explanation reliability.
scope_and_methods: Read the official arXiv v2 HTML. The controlled paired audit holds an image fixed while changing provenance metadata and tests multiple medical-imaging datasets/modalities and VLMs. An explicit AI-origin tag reduced accuracy on authentic images by 61.1% on average. The proposed SAVC pipeline uses counterfactual verification to detect and neutralize provenance shortcuts.
observed_reliability_evidence: This is direct evidence that multimodal authenticity decisions can over-weight provenance text, and that counterfactual interventions can expose decision shortcuts. The paper does not evaluate the factual correctness, visual grounding, causal faithfulness, or stability of a generated explanation; its paired verdict consistency is not an explanation-quality measure.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Useful for system-level robustness and appropriate-reliance framing, especially because a source tag can override visual evidence, but not direct evidence about forensic explanations. The paper notes its provenance conditions are a controlled spectrum rather than a full simulation of clinical records and does not systematically evaluate prompt sensitivity.
screening_conclusion: Retain as an adjacent multimodal deployment-risk study and keep separate from intrinsic explanation-reliability evidence. The Scholar conference-title card and arXiv v2 are two versions of one work identity.

paper: CIFAKE: Image Classification and Explainable Identification of AI-Generated Synthetic Images
verified_identity: Jordan J. Bird & Ahmad Lotfi; CIFAKE: Image Classification and Explainable Identification of AI-Generated Synthetic Images; arXiv:2303.14126v1 (2023), later IEEE Access 2024.
relevance_class: Direct AI-generated-image detection with Grad-CAM visualization; explanation reliability not established.
scope_and_methods: Read the complete official arXiv HTML. CIFAKE contains 120,000 32×32 images (60,000 CIFAR-10 real and 60,000 Stable Diffusion 1.4 generated); CNNs are trained for real-versus-generated classification and Grad-CAM is applied to selected images. The best reported classification accuracy is 92.98% (the complete trained model’s reported validation maximum is 93.55%).
observed_reliability_evidence: Grad-CAM examples are interpreted visually: the authors say generated-image decisions often focus on sparse background imperfections and that the depicted entity itself has little activation. The paper does not compare heatmaps with independent artifact annotations, run explanation sanity checks/causal interventions, ask people to judge explanation correctness, report inter-rater agreement, or test appropriate user reliance.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: This is a direct early XAI application to AI-generated-image detection, not a validation study of explanation reliability. Detection accuracy, dataset scale, fixed seeds, and plausible heatmaps cannot establish causal faithfulness or factual evidence grounding. The paper’s 32×32 CIFAR-aligned images also constrain external validity to modern high-resolution forensic settings.
screening_conclusion: Upgrade the pre-existing 90/72 candidate to a targeted official full-text review in 172; reuse its previous identity and do not count it again as a new discovery.

paper: Can ChatGPT Detect DeepFakes? A Study of Using Multimodal Large Language Models for Media Forensics
verified_identity: Shan Jia et al.; CVPR 2024 workshop paper; arXiv:2403.14077v4 (2024-06-11).
relevance_class: 强相关问题动机/任务邻接：多模态LLM图像鉴伪解释可能与实际支持证据脱节。
scope_and_methods: 定向核读arXiv v4全文§§1–5。评估GPT-4V与Gemini 1.0 Pro在1,000张FFHQ真实人脸及2,000张DF3合成人脸（StyleGAN2、Latent Diffusion）上的真假判断；Prompt #6要求判断合成伪迹并以[region, artifacts]形式解释。含JPEG压缩、模糊、融合及对抗等后处理。
observed_reliability_evidence: 作者在§3图例后明确指出：部分yes/no判断正确，但支撑证据并不正确（§3，arXiv HTML行130）。§4.2还报告GPT-4V会将真实图像中的少见语义特征误读为合成伪迹，Gemini的伪迹分析缺乏合理性（行173–175）。这是直接的定性错证案例；论文未报告错误解释的系统比例或独立解释评分。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 主要终点是检测AUC、准确率与拒答率（例如Prompt #6在StyleGAN2上的拒答率4.7%、非拒答样本准确率83.83%），不是解释效度指标。未见独立伪迹真值对解释逐条核验、解释盲评/评分者一致性、删除插入或参数随机化等faithfulness测试，也未研究用户适当依赖。定性错证案例不能外推为总体错误率；检测表现不能代替解释可靠性。
screening_conclusion: 保留为强相关问题动机和早期任务论文：它直接展示判决与自然语言证据可能脱节；不把它描述成已经量化验证解释faithfulness的基准研究。身份复用EFR-REF012和M2F2-Det-REF-28，不计新发现。

paper: MGFFD-VLM: Multi-Granularity Prompt Learning for Face Forgery Detection with VLM
verified_identity: Tao Chen, Jingyi Zhang, Decheng Liu, Chunlei Peng; ACM Web Conference 2026 paper (Scholar card DOI 10.1145/3774904.3792220); arXiv:2507.12232v1, posted 2025-07-16.
relevance_class: 直接面部深伪解释方法；解释效度验证有限，强相关。
scope_and_methods: 定向核读官方arXiv v1全文（§§1–5）。提出DD-VQA+、MobileVLM-based MGFFD-VLM及多粒度提示，输出真假判断、伪造区域/类型和人脸质量属性。训练含图像级标签、可用时的像素级篡改mask监督、对比损失及文本标签校准；在DD-VQA+上评检测分类与答案生成，并报告Celeb-DF、DFDC、WildDeepfake检测AUC。
observed_reliability_evidence: 存在一定位置接地机制：主文称伪造分割mask用于训练，在有mask时采用像素CE；答案生成报告BLEU-4、CIDEr、ROUGE-L、METEOR、SPICE。模型检测Acc=.9072/F1=.9420，语言指标ROUGE-L=.6963、SPICE=.6629。主文定性展示其指出皮肤纹理或融合边界。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 训练mask监督与分类性能不等于生成解释通过独立证据核验。语言重叠分数不直接测主张真值、区域充分/必要性或决策因果faithfulness；主文未报告解释claim逐项核实、面向独立真值的解释幻觉率、人类解释质量/一致性、删除插入/参数随机化或appropriate-reliance实验。主文评测协议主要列检测Acc/Recall/Precision/F1、语言指标和外部检测AUC；未找到独立定位解释效度指标。
screening_conclusion: 纳入直接强相关图像鉴伪解释方法；说明训练和生成接口含位置提示/mask，但不把mask监督或文本相似度分数描述成已证明解释可靠。版本按arXiv与ACM DOI合并。

paper: Employing Vision-Language Models for Face Image Quality Assessment
verified_identity: Erdi Sarıtaş, Eren Onaran, Vitomir Štruc, Hazım Kemal Ekenel; arXiv:2605.17489v1 (2026-05-17); IEEE FG 2026 camera-ready metadata appears in author-hosted conference PDF.
relevance_class: 强方法邻接：面部图像解释的事实性/幻觉、内部一致性与prompt稳健性；非鉴伪任务。
scope_and_methods: 核读官方arXiv v1全文。多种开源VLM在CelebA-HQ、LFW、IJB-B、SCFace上做zero-shot face image quality assessment；prompt要求输出质量分及blur、resolution、lighting、compression属性。合成Mix Degradation基准对干净图和已知5类退化标签使用受控退化，并报告clean-image false-positive/hallucination、hard-artifact recall、Hamming distance；另以MAE/Pearson及标签—分数关系衡量prompt与内部一致性。
observed_reliability_evidence: 在干净图上QWEN2.5-32B约49.1%会报告至少一种不存在的退化，而QWEN2.5-7B有87.9%干净图报告零退化。混合退化中，7B识别hard artifact召回79.8%、完整识别3种退化39.7%；32B分别62.0%和8.7%。更大模型可保持评分—标签高度单调一致，却仍在干净样本频繁幻觉，直接展示自洽不等于事实正确；较小模型对prompt语义更敏感。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 目标是图像质量退化标签，不是图像来源真实性/伪造类别；合成退化基准覆盖blur/noise/低分辨率/JPEG/曝光，不代表真实取证伪造线索。没有用户研究或适当依赖测试，也未对模型内部因果faithfulness做干预。其定量ground-truth tag protocol可迁移作邻近方法参照，但不能直接当作鉴伪解释的域内效度结果。
screening_conclusion: 作为强方法邻接保留：提供可迁移的解释标签真值核验、hallucination与prompt-consistency维度，并实证区分自洽和准确；明确不计作图像鉴伪直接实证。

paper: A lightweight dual-branch spatial-frequency framework for joint deepfake detection and localization
verified_identity: Duc Viet Bui, Tung Duong Tran, Huu Dao Tran, Van Kien Dinh, Duc Cuong Pham, Tuan Linh Dang; Computer Vision and Image Understanding 270 (2026), 104860; DOI 10.1016/j.cviu.2026.104860.
relevance_class: 直接深伪检测/区域定位任务候选；当前仅出版社摘要核查。
scope_and_methods: 仅核Google Scholar题录和ScienceDirect官方摘要/Highlights。DBDD用空间与频域双分支共同检测面部伪造，并生成篡改区域mask；摘要称在FF++、Celeb-DF v2、DFD及跨数据集/压缩设置下评估。

paper: Evidence-Grounded Forensic Reasoning for Detecting and Grounding Multi-Modal Media Manipulation
relevance_class: 直接核心：跨模态图像鉴伪解释的空间/文本接地与评价构念边界。
scope_and_methods: 2026-10-15 re-read of official arXiv HTML §§1–5 and Tables 1–4, confirming the existing full-text review: Anchor-and-Verify puts predicted coordinates/token spans in the hypothesis block, separates visual and text perception before conflict analysis, and binds evidence to the predicted face box/text span. The five deterministic reward components cover format, hierarchical classification, face localization, text localization, and reasoning consistency; token-level MDA routes task-specific advantages. A 50K reasoning set is generated by an MLLM conditioned on ground-truth findings, then filtered by rules, independent MLLM review, and manual review of flagged cases. All 56 printed bibliography items were screened separately in 03/T466; close direct citations have individual source notes in 169.
observed_reliability_evidence: The paper enforces spatial/token overlap and internal evidence-conclusion consistency during training. §4.4 evaluates reasoning only on correctly predicted manipulated samples: NLI coherence 38.73→41.07 (+2.34), redundancy 0.35→0.22, ROUGE-L 42.99→43.56, Distinct-2 8.99→9.21 and Distinct-3 18.99→19.31 (SFT→MDPO). These are automatic text/consistency properties under the stated condition; they do not independently prove each claim is visually true or that the detector causally relied on the cited evidence.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Ground-truth-conditioned rationale generation and coordinate/token overlap constraints may introduce generation/annotation dependence; MLLM-generated labels plus manual inspection of flagged cases do not establish that every training rationale was independently human-verified. §4.4 conditions text metrics on correctly predicted manipulated samples, omitting authentic images and detector errors. Main text reports no independent blind human rating of model outputs, inter-rater reliability, claim-level visual-support rate over a representative test set, appropriate-reliance/user study, counterfactual deletion/insertion, parameter randomization, or other causal-faithfulness intervention. Spatial consistency and NLI coherence are useful but distinct constructs.
screening_conclusion: Direct strong-core candidate for evidence-grounded multimodal forensic explanation and its validity boundaries. Official full text re-read 2026-10-15 and screening status updated; the work presents a grounding mechanism and limited automatic reasoning-quality measures, not comprehensive independent explanation-reliability validation or appropriate-reliance evidence.

paper: SNIPPET: A Framework for Subjective Evaluation of Visual Explanations Applied to DeepFake Detection
verified_identity: Yuqing Yang, Boris Joukovsky, José Antonio Oramas Mogrovejo, Tinne Tuytelaars, Nikos Deligiannis; ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications 20(8), article 253 (2024), pp. 1–29; DOI 10.1145/3665248. VUB official accepted-author-manuscript record and PDF.
relevance_class: 直接强相关的人类主观解释评价原始研究；偏可理解性、偏好和人类线索对齐，不等于解释客观可靠性。
scope_and_methods: 沿用此前对VUB 29页accepted author manuscript §§4–8的已记录核读范围（72现有条目）；本轮重新核实VUB正式出版元数据、摘要/引文关系，不声称今天重新通读全稿。研究以ViT-B深伪检测器比较Grad-CAM、LRP、Attention Rollout、Transformer Attribution；按经验组招募161名志愿者，记录1,542次选择/评价和562个区域标注。用户在识别正确或错误情境下比较解释；解释区域与用户区域标注的相似度/相关性另作自动评价，文中报告对一个70例的合成标注子集进行SIM/Pearson比较。
observed_reliability_evidence: 方法间存在用户偏好及群体差异证据：Attention Rollout总体更受偏好，但不同经验层的解释偏好和感知帮助程度不同；可见并已记录的实验也比较热图与用户所标区域的一致性。这些结果对解释的可感知性、人机匹配和人评设计有直接价值，并暴露“用户喜欢/觉得帮助”会随经验改变。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 用户偏好/主观帮助感、与人类注意区域的重合、以及模型实际决策因果faithfulness是不同构念。用户区域不是独立法证伪迹或模型因果证据真值；标注任务仅部分条件/正确作答者参与并有样本和矩形框局限。现有记录未见报告多评审IAA/独立证据真值、人为扰动对照、删除/插入或参数随机化sanity check、对真实调查决策的appropriate-reliance测试。故不能从高偏好或人类区域重合推出解释事实准确或因果忠实。
screening_conclusion: 纳入强相关核心清单，是本主题最直接的人类主观解释评价工作之一；结论限于偏好、感知有用性、用户组差异与人类区域对齐。把主观可用性证据与客观/因果效度、适当依赖分开报告。

paper: Interpol review of detection of AI-generated image and video deepfakes, 2022-2025
verified_identity: Stijn van Lierop, Ivona Najdenkoska, Marcel Worring, Zeno Geradts; Forensic Science International: Synergy 13 (2026), article 100704; DOI 10.1016/j.fsisyn.2026.100704; PMID 42326391; PMCID PMC13279904.
relevance_class: 强相关法证场景综述/检索地图；主题邻接，非解释可靠性原始实验。
scope_and_methods: 定向核读可访问PMC全文§§1–2、6–7及结论，尤其引用SNIPPET的参考文献[321]。作者称分析400余项2022-01-01至2025-06-01研究；数据库检索Scopus、IEEE Digital Library、ACM Digital Library，并手动从Google Scholar和相关参考文献补入。综述聚焦至少一种模态完全AI生成的图像/视频，并说明既有媒体操纵与全合成媒体之间有连续谱但采用偏全合成范围。
observed_reliability_evidence: 综述总结视觉CAM/Transformer attention可指出影响模型预测的图像区域，但不能给出为何重要的实际解释；扰动式SHAP/LIME删除/插入可能引入新伪迹而造成不一致；引用SNIPPET报告Rollout更受人偏好，但视觉图本身仍不足以说明预测理由，XAI还可能通过选择性聚焦影响用户。作者将解释与法证证据评价框架列为未来方向。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 该综述没有对解释方法运行新的人评、因果faithfulness、独立伪迹真值或appropriate-reliance实验；所述结论是对已发表研究的综合。主要研究范围是完全AI生成媒体，明确排除许多对既有媒体的操纵研究；覆盖时间也截至2025-06，不能视作全图像篡改鉴伪综述或全领域穷尽搜索。
screening_conclusion: 作为强相关背景与引文地图纳入90/72/172；其第6节可支持区分热图、可解释性主张与法证证据充分性。必须限定为合成媒体和综述级证据，不能说该文验证了某种解释的可靠性。

paper: ProtoExplorer: Interpretable Forensic Analysis of Deepfake Videos using Prototype Exploration and Refinement
verified_identity: M. den Bouter, J. L. Pardo, Z. Geradts, M. Worring; Information Visualization 23(3), 2024, 239-257; DOI 10.1177/14738716241238476; arXiv:2309.11155
relevance_class: Direct forensic explanation and human-factors neighbor; video rather than still-image task
scope_and_methods: Official arXiv HTML reviewed for research question, system, expert study, results and discussion. Prototype exploration/refinement for deepfake video analysis; N=5 Netherlands Forensic Institute experts, each with >9 years of experience; think-aloud sessions and interviews/follow-up feedback.
observed_reliability_evidence: The expert evaluation surfaced concrete explanation limitations: prototypes did not cover all face regions; regions compared across categories were not always comparable; optical-flow displays were difficult to interpret; interpolated activation maps lacked clarity/spatial precision and were replaced by PRP maps. This is qualitative evidence about interpretability and expert feedback, not a calibrated explanation-accuracy score.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The paper does not establish pixel/claim ground truth for explanations, causal faithfulness, parameter-randomization sanity, deletion/insertion or counterfactual necessity/sufficiency, inter-rater reliability, measured forensic decision accuracy improvement, or appropriate reliance. The small expert sample supports formative human-factors conclusions only. Video-task evidence is adjacent to still-image forgery.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a high-priority human-factors/forensic explanation neighbor and as evidence that visual explanations can be incomplete or spatially unclear; do not label it as a quantitative explanation-reliability benchmark.

paper: Sparse Prototype-Based Framework for Deepfake Detection Using Class-Specific Dictionary Learning
verified_identity: Fatima Khalid, Usman Haider, Muhammad Hanif, Ahmar Rashid, Akhtar Khalil; IEEE Access 13 (2025), 204402-204415; DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3636276
relevance_class: Direct deepfake prototype/dictionary explanation method; adjacent to explanation reliability, not validated reliability evidence
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the public author-accepted full text's method, comparison/interpretability discussion, limitations and references. InceptionResNetV2 embeddings feed class-specific sparse dictionaries; Orthogonal Matching Pursuit coefficients and class reconstruction residuals drive classification. Evaluated on Celeb-DF and five FaceForensics++ manipulation subsets.
observed_reliability_evidence: The authors describe predictions as traceable through sparse coefficients/prototypes and assign their model moderate interpretability scores (5-7/10) under author-defined criteria: architectural transparency, prediction traceability, and literature evidence. The score is an author judgment, not an independent human or ground-truth reliability measure.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The text explicitly reports no human-centered validation or perceptual evaluation and leaves user studies/expert feedback for future work. No independent explanation ground truth, causal faithfulness, randomization sanity checks, deletion/insertion, counterfactual necessity/sufficiency, inter-rater agreement, or appropriate-reliance outcome was identified. The public copy contains at least three reference-identifier mismatches (#11, #14, #17), recorded separately; its bibliography heading says 25 although numbered references run [1]-[26].
screening_conclusion: Add to the direct-task method neighborhood because it makes intrinsic interpretability claims for deepfake detection; do not treat its self-assigned score as validated reliability. Preserve the three bibliography mismatches as unresolved rather than silently repairing them.

paper: PUDD: Towards Robust Multi-modal Prototype-based Deepfake Detection
verified_identity: Alvaro Lopez Pellicer, Yi Li, Plamen Angelov; CVPR Workshops 2024 (DFAD), pp. 3809-3817; DOI 10.1109/CVPRW63382.2024.00385; arXiv:2406.15921v2
relevance_class: Direct prototype-based deepfake video and synthetic-image detection/explanation method; adjacent to explanation reliability, not validated reliability evidence
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the official arXiv v2 full text (research question, method, evaluation, visualization, interpretability, discussion and references). PUDD compares DINOv2 feature representations with class prototypes and similarity scores, then applies a rule-based threshold; it shows linguistic/prototype explanation examples. Detection accuracy is reported as 95.1% on Celeb-DF video frames and 94.6% on CIFAKE synthetic images. All 40 numbered bibliography positions were separately screened by title/topic.
observed_reliability_evidence: The paper defines interpretability as the degree to which a human can consistently predict the model output and presents prototype similarity plus a rule-based linguistic representation. It does not report a human prediction/interpretation study or a measured explanation-reliability outcome. The accuracy figures measure detector classification, not explanation reliability. A qualitative missed video is attributed to frequent eye closure, but this is not an explanation-ground-truth test.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: No independent explanation ground truth, claim/evidence grounding score, causal faithfulness, parameter-randomization sanity check, deletion/insertion or counterfactual sufficiency/necessity, explanation agreement, or appropriate-reliance evaluation was identified in the reviewed text. The method targets video and image detection, but interpretability evidence is an illustrative prototype/rule display; robustness and accuracy cannot substitute for explanation reliability.
screening_conclusion: Retain the pre-existing 90/72 identity as a direct method neighbor and upgrade its status with full-text evidence. Do not present PUDD as empirical support that image-forgery explanations are reliable.

paper: Artifact magnification on deepfake videos increases human detection and subjective confidence
verified_identity: Emilie Josephs, Camilo Fosco, Aude Oliva; arXiv:2304.04733 (2023 preprint); DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2304.04733
relevance_class: Human-AI decision-support and visual-evidence neighbor in deepfake video; relevant to reliance/confidence, not a conventional explanation-fidelity study
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the 10-page official arXiv PDF, focusing on the ecological viewing-condition experiment, artifact-amplification study, Study 2 design/results, and limitations. A human-annotation-trained artifact map guides motion magnification to create visibly distorted deepfake videos. The paper reports 913 participants across all Study 1 sub-experiments (while another summary passage says 180 per condition across five conditions); Study 2 reports 298 participants and measures model-suggestion acceptance, final confidence, and confidence change when comparing text feedback with artifact caricatures.
observed_reliability_evidence: The visual indicator improved fake-video hit rates across the tested viewing conditions; in Study 2 the visual condition led to higher confidence than text feedback on medium/hard videos and the paper measures whether participants accept advice. This is decision-support evidence, not validation of whether the highlighted regions are faithful explanations. Crucially, Study 2's displayed predictions were set to ground truth (a 100%-accurate 'model'), so it estimates best-case acceptance and does not test appropriate reliance when the model is wrong.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The task is manipulated video rather than still-image forgery; artifact magnification changes the stimulus and is not a conventional explanation overlay. Perfect ground-truth feedback in Study 2 excludes model-error calibration and cannot establish appropriate reliance under realistic errors. No independent explanation truth, causal faithfulness, explanation-rating agreement, or localization accuracy of a displayed explanation was evaluated. It is a 2023 preprint in the same research line as Deepfake Caricatures (arXiv:2206.00535); whether any participants or datasets overlap is not established here, so do not count it as an independent replication without checking versions/materials.
screening_conclusion: Add as a strong adjacent human-factors result that helps specify the reliance/confidence construct and a boundary condition for the review; do not treat it as direct image-forgery explanation reliability evidence or as proof of appropriate reliance.

paper: The Value of AI Guidance in Human Examination of Synthetically-Generated Faces
verified_identity: Aidan Boyd, Patrick Tinsley, Kevin Bowyer, Adam Czajka; Proceedings of AAAI 2023, 37(5), 5930-5938; DOI 10.1609/aaai.v37i5.25734; arXiv:2208.10544
relevance_class: Direct synthetic-face authenticity task with model-saliency presentation and human decision outcomes; highly relevant human evaluation, not a causal-faithfulness benchmark
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the official 9-page AAAI proceedings PDF and official article record. More than 1,560 participants classified authentic versus synthetic faces and marked decision-support regions across no-AI, model-decision, CAM-only, and decision+CAM conditions. Six GAN sources were represented. The paper reports a count discrepancy: the abstract says 56,015 annotations; the body reports 45,232 annotations from 1,260 annotators plus 10,833 additional annotations for 1,560 subjects, totaling 56,065.
observed_reliability_evidence: CAM-only and decision+CAM conditions remained around 56% mean accuracy; decision-only was about 59%, and the human-guided model pairing about 61%. The within-subject null of no accuracy gain was not rejected for CAM-only (p=.315) or CAM+decision (p=.369), but was rejected for decision-only (p=.011). Human annotations showed greater similarity to CAMs from human-guided models; when CAM and decision were both shown, agreement with the AI was generally higher. The authors note that seeing what the AI thinks and why could increase confidence in the AI and lower accuracy when the model is relatively inaccurate.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Human saliency annotation overlap is agreement about attended regions, not independent authenticity/forgery ground truth. The study measures human task performance and agreement/trust but does not test causal faithfulness by interventions, parameter randomization, deletion/insertion, claim-level factuality, or calibrated reliance under model error as a primary endpoint. CAM display was not useful for accuracy in this task; findings depend on synthetic-face detection and should not be equated with localization of edited regions in composite images. The annotation-total discrepancy is retained rather than silently normalized.
screening_conclusion: Add as a strong direct human-evaluation/AI-guidance study and a warning that CAM agreement or perceived explanation can raise trust without improving accuracy. Treat explanation validity, user utility, and appropriate reliance as separate constructs.

paper: Deepfake detection by human crowds, machines, and machine-informed crowds
verified_identity: Matthew Groh, Ziv Epstein, Chaz Firestone, Rosalind Picard; Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 119(1), e2110013119 (2022); DOI 10.1073/pnas.2110013119
relevance_class: Direct deepfake video human-AI decision and appropriate-reliance neighbor; no explanation intervention
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the official PNAS open article (abstract, study design, results, discussion and conclusions). Two online studies with 15,016 participants compare ordinary observers with a leading computer-vision detector; Experiment 2 exposes participants to model predictions and measures response updates/confidence on held-out videos.
observed_reliability_evidence: The authors report that pooled human+model decisions can outperform either alone, but inaccurate model predictions often decrease human accuracy. In their held-out video analysis, participants frequently adjusted their judgments after model advice, and inaccurate or equivocal model predictions led them astray in 8 of 10 instances. The paper explicitly frames decision-support systems as needing to weigh human and model predictions appropriately.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: This is decision-level reliance evidence, not an explainability study: no saliency map, textual rationale, independent evidence ground truth for explanations, or explanation-quality measure is tested. The study uses deepfake video and a particular DFDC-era model/stimuli; it informs failure modes and experimental design but does not establish any explanation's faithfulness or transfer to still-image splicing/tampering.
screening_conclusion: Include as a high-value neighboring human-AI reliance study to ground the risk of following wrong forensic decisions; keep separate from direct explanation-reliability evidence.

paper: The eyes know it: FakeET- An Eye-tracking Database to Understand Deepfake Perception
verified_identity: Parul Gupta, Komal Chugh, Abhinav Dhall, Ramanathan Subramanian; ACM ICMI 2020, pp. 519-527; DOI 10.1145/3382507.3418857; arXiv:2006.06961
relevance_class: Human visual-attention and deepfake-video localization resource; adjacent evidence, not a model-explanation validity evaluation
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the official 9-page arXiv full text and publication metadata from Monash University. The dataset records eye gaze/EEG from 40 participants viewing 811 Google/Jigsaw deepfake videos (331 real, 480 fake); the authors analyze gaze differences, gaze saliency maps, and whether gaze inputs improve detection.
observed_reliability_evidence: The paper reports gaze-map utility for spatial forgery localization/detection and approximately 5% detection-performance improvement when gaze maps are used as model inputs. Participants fixated more around manipulated faces in fake videos. These findings support human-attention maps as a possible contextual reference for forensic systems.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Gaze is an implicit attention label, not necessarily a true manipulation mask or a correct causal reason for a detector. The paper does not compare a model explanation to independent pixel-level evidence truth, test explanation randomization/faithfulness, report explanation-rater agreement, or assess whether users appropriately rely on model advice. It focuses on video face manipulations and a small participant sample.
screening_conclusion: Include as an adjacent human-grounding resource; do not use eye gaze as a sufficient gold standard for explanation fidelity or artifact truth.

paper: On Human Predictions with Explanations and Predictions of Machine Learning Models: A Case Study on Deception Detection
relevance_class: Cross-domain methodological precedent on explanation presentation, human agency and reliance; textual deceptive-review task
scope_and_methods: Reviewed the official arXiv v4 full text, DOI metadata, experimental setup, results and discussion. A between-subject Mechanical Turk study uses deceptive versus genuine hotel reviews and varies control, feature explanations alone, example explanations, model labels, accuracy claims, and combinations. Each setup has 80 participants; a linear SVM reaches 87% held-out accuracy.
observed_reliability_evidence: Explanations alone yield only a slight human-accuracy improvement; showing predicted labels yields about a 21% relative improvement over control, and adding explanations to a label can have a similar effect to a strong stated accuracy cue. The paper measures trust as the proportion of cases following the model and reports more trust in correct than incorrect predictions, though the difference is statistically significant in only some setups. It exposes a performance/agency tradeoff relevant to appropriate-reliance study design.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The task is text-based review deception, not image or video forensics. Feature heatmaps over words are not visual saliency explanations. Model agreement/trust does not by itself equal appropriate reliance; its findings cannot establish that a forensic explanation is factually grounded or causally faithful, nor can they be transferred quantitatively to image-authenticity judgments.
screening_conclusion: Keep as a clearly labeled cross-domain methodological neighbor for designing human explanation/reliance experiments; exclude from counts of direct image-forgery explanation studies.

paper: Non-identifiability of Explanations from Model Behavior in Deep Networks of Image Authenticity Judgments
verified_identity: Icaro Re Depaolini and Uri Hasson; arXiv:2604.07254v1 [cs.CV], posted 2026-04-08; no peer-reviewed venue identified on the reviewed arXiv record.
relevance_class: Methodological neighbor on explanation stability and non-identifiability for models of subjective image-authenticity judgments; explicitly not an objective image-forensics study.
scope_and_methods: Read the official arXiv v1 HTML: abstract, §§1–6, methods, results, discussion, limitations, conclusions, and the linked citation trail. The study uses AIGCIQA2023 human authenticity ratings for AI-generated images. It removes 1,033 of 2,400 images by prompt-metadata rules and models the remaining 1,367 using frozen pretrained vision backbones plus regression heads across 10 random seeds/splits. It compares Grad-CAM, LIME, and multiscale pixel masking within and across six architectures. Authenticity ratings come from 25 participants; the paper estimates human split-half reliability and a noise ceiling.
observed_reliability_evidence: Corrected split-half reliability of human authenticity ratings is 0.67 (estimated noise ceiling ≈0.82); quality and authenticity ratings correlate r=0.84. Model prediction vectors across seeds have pairwise reliability r=0.81–0.91, yet explanation maps can vary across seeds (e.g., Grad-CAM top-5% IoU is 0.41 for DenseNet161 and 0.46 for EfficientNetB3, versus 0.77–0.81 for several other architectures). Across-architecture attribution agreement is generally weak or low-to-moderate despite similar predictive performance. VGG16/VGG19 predict authenticity largely through quality-shared variance (partial r=0.01/0.03, not significant), showing that performance and reproducibility do not establish construct-valid evidence. LIME surrogate fidelity is moderate (R²≈0.43–0.60).
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The authors explicitly distinguish their target—subjective human ratings of how real AI-generated images appear—from objective real/fake image forensics. Consistency is a reliability property, not independent evidence that a heatmap identifies objectively true forensic cues or is causally faithful. The study does not test user-facing explanation comprehension, trust calibration, or appropriate reliance, and it does not provide independently adjudicated forensic artifact masks/claims. The authors state they did not perform formal explanation sanity/fragility analyses. Frozen backbones mean seed stability measures regression-head/readout stability, not whole-architecture retraining stability. In the explanation-set experiment, channel pruning uses the test/explanation set; the paper cautions those results cannot be treated as generalization. The results therefore inform evaluation design and the limits of explanation consistency, not direct claims about forensic detectors.
screening_conclusion: Keep as a high-value methodological neighbor on image-authenticity explanation reliability; do not count it as direct image-forgery/deepfake explanation validation or human appropriate-reliance evidence. Keep priority rank 57 unchanged after full-text review.

paper: TRIDENT: Tri-modal Deepfake Perception, Detection, and Hallucination Grand Challenge
verified_identity: Wen-Huang Cheng, Hong-Han Shuai, Khoa Doan, Hongxia Xie, Ling Lo, Jian-Yu Jiang-Lin, Kang-Yang Huang, Ling Zou; ACM Multimedia 2026 Grand Challenge report; official program title omits 'Grand'; listed for Nov 11, 2026. OpenReview forum id H7hsRMzu7B.
relevance_class: 直接相关邻接：图像鉴伪解释的人工伪迹证据接地、无支持claim/幻觉评测（多模态挑战）
scope_and_methods: 部分文本核读（不是完整PDF逐页核读）。ACM官方计划摘要称该挑战建立在TriDF benchmark上，图像/视频/音频分别排名，评Perception、Detection、Hallucination Robustness，并以结构化VQA与开放式推理共同测量；吸引21队注册，三轨共99次提交。挑战网页列出TFQ/MCQ、已知伪造样本的Type-A解释、未知真伪样本的Type-B判定+理由。论文PDF索引片段给出：Cover为LLM抽取artifact claims与人工真值伪迹的重合/覆盖；CHAIR为已报告伪迹中不支持项的比例；F0.5以非幻觉率作precision、coverage作recall并偏重precision；空解释设CHAIR=1、F0.5=0。挑战总分TCS=0.4 Detection + 0.3 Hallucination Robustness + 0.3 Perception，按模态宏平均。
observed_reliability_evidence: ACM官方日程摘要报告21个注册队伍与99次跨track提交，并称高检测准确率并不保证强伪迹感知/解释接地；获胜方法共同采用专门的取证感知、证据引导的多模态推理和显式控制unsupported claims。该结果为挑战级经验观察；当前核得的公开摘要没有按图像track列出完整分数或置信区间。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: 自由文本由LLM解析并映射到离散伪迹集合，结果依赖映射器与taxonomy；已访问的官方摘要/挑战页未报告映射准确率、独立人类复核、标注者一致性、校准曲线或错误分层。人工伪迹真值提供外部接地锚点，但Cover/CHAIR仍是taxonomy相对的claim支持代理，不能证明模型决策因果依赖该证据、反事实必要/充分性、解释跨扰动稳定性或人类appropriate reliance。图像轨应与视频/音频结果分开。OpenReview论坛/PDF在Chrome打开时显示浏览器验证；本条只记录官方摘要/挑战页及索引可见片段，待直连全文成功后再补充，不冒充完整原文核读。
screening_conclusion: 保留为直接相关的解释接地/幻觉评价基准，适合综述中‘解释内容是否得到观测伪迹支持’一类证据；需要与因果忠实性、解释鲁棒性及用户信赖校准分开编码。当前为部分原稿核对，完整全文效度审查仍待完成。

paper: Explainability-Guided Deepfake Detection for High-Fidelity Facial Edits
verified_identity: Bibek Das; Soumi Chattopadhyay; Chandranath Adak; Astitva Pandey; Ashutosh Parihar; Zahid Akhtar; Soumya Dutta; Abdenour Hadid; ICPR 2026 conference paper, Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 16815, pp. 496–511; First Online 2026-08-03; DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-31663-9_33. Springer copyright year 2027 is distinct from online date.
relevance_class: 直接强相关：高保真面部编辑鉴伪中解释空间接地/faithfulness与视角/扰动稳健性
scope_and_methods: 摘要级核读；Springer章节全文受订阅限制。出版商摘要称Side-VLM为多视角、最小面部编辑数据集，含像素级篡改mask，用于联合评估检测和解释faithfulness；还称VLM具有视角敏感、prompt依赖，常规检测器可关注背景/偶然区域；作者提出CAM与GT篡改mask显式对齐的训练方式。摘要未给样本数、生成/标注协议、数据切分、基线或具体解释指标。
observed_reliability_evidence: 仅能确认摘要报告的结论：摘要声称解释引导训练在挑战视角和常见图像扰动下改善检测鲁棒性与解释faithfulness。本次未获得全文中的量化数值、方差/置信区间或统计检验，因此这些目前是经正式出版商摘要核实的作者主张，不是独立复算/完整效度核读。
limitations_and_construct_boundary: CAM/掩码空间重合可支持定位/接地评价，但单靠对齐训练及扰动结果不能证明固定模型决策对解释区域具有因果必要性/充分性。目前无法核faithfulness定义与具体分数，亦未从摘要见人类独立解释事实审查、评分者一致性、appropriate-reliance实验或用户结果。主题限面部身份保持编辑，迁移到拼接、copy-move或文档/卫星图像需另证。正文受订阅限制；此记录严格为摘要级。
screening_conclusion: 直接强相关且优先级高，适合纳入解释可靠性综述中空间接地与扰动稳健性路线；目前只有正式摘要证据，全文中的faithfulness操作定义、评测结果和验证协议仍待取得，不能归为已完成全文核读。

paper: DDL: Effective and Comprehensible Interpretation Framework for Diverse Deepfake Detectors
verified_identity: Zekun Sun, Na Ruan, Jianhua Li; IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security, vol. 20, pp. 3601–3615 (2025); DOI 10.1109/TIFS.2025.3553803. DOI/title and venue metadata were cross-checked against DBLP and the Shanghai Jiao Tong University faculty publication list.

paper: Detection of Images Generated by Multi-Modal Models

relevance_class: 直接强相关灰色文献：图像深伪检测解释方法，并实测多类解释可靠性代理指标及人类感知/改判影响；不是同行评审论文。
scope_and_methods: 全文核读：XAI evaluation §2.3.4 (PDF pp.51–65) and study design/results; seven methods RISE, SOBOL, XRAI, Anchors, SeCAM, DFT-CAM, DFT-CAM+XRAI, applied to RINE detector. Metric tests include deletion of high-importance regions and detector accuracy drop; deletion of least-important regions and SSIM change; Gaussian noise and resolution sensitivity; repeated runs; demographic-group explanation overlap. Human study: 6 participants, 8 image-decision tasks each, model label plus six visual explanations, 288 rating observations; ratings cover helpfulness/trust and opinion change.
observed_reliability_evidence: The report operationalizes explanation tests beyond visualization: high-score deletion changes detector accuracy; low-score deletion estimates map stability with SSIM; noise/resolution changes and repeated explanation runs probe sensitivity/reproducibility; group-level map overlap probes demographic consistency. Results are method- and setting-dependent: DFT-CAM/hybrid are reported relatively robust under higher noise; RISE/Anchors overlap changes after more low-importance-region deletion; group-overlap differs between fake-only and mixed real/fake samples. In the small user study, DFT-CAM had mean helpfulness 2.75 and trust 3.32 (5-point scale); DFT-CAM+XRAI and XRAI each changed opinions in 6/48 trials (12.5%), while higher persuasion did not track higher trust/helpfulness.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The paper's 'accuracy' test measures detector-performance drop after deleting salient pixels; it does not measure whether a textual/spatial explanation is factually correct against independent forensic evidence. The stability/fairness tests use SSIM/overlap proxies on small selected sets; they do not establish causal necessity/sufficiency, parameter-randomization sanity, or validity under acquisition/compression shifts. The human study is exploratory (6 participants); opinion change/persuasion is not appropriate reliance, and the report does not show whether changed decisions became more accurate, report confidence calibration, or compare explanations to expert-grounded evidence. The report is gray literature and concerns AI-generated-image/deepfake detection; do not generalize to all manipulations (splicing, copy-move, document, satellite) without evidence.
screening_conclusion: Strongly relevant because it directly evaluates explanation robustness-related properties and human response in image-deepfake detection. Treat its measured proxy results as reported evidence, with limited construct validity; no claim that it proves explanation faithfulness or appropriate reliance. A separate 2026 CVPRW paper from the project team remains inaccessible and is not covered by this review.

paper: Trainable Noise Model as an Explainable Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Method: Application on Sobol for Remote Sensing Image Segmentation

paper: Trustworthy forgery detection with causal inference
verified_identity: Junxian Duan, Fan Ji, Yi Li, Hao Sun, Ran He; Letter; Science China Information Sciences, 68(6), article 160108, 2025; published 21 May 2025; DOI 10.1007/s11432-024-4347-6
relevance_class: Adjacent: causal/interpretable forensic forgery-detection method; not direct explanation-validity evidence
scope_and_methods: Full 2-page publisher PDF and all 4 supplementary pages reviewed. The letter models forgery detection with an SCM, decomposes encoder features into forgery-pattern Zn and forgery-irrelevant Zp, and adds FBEM, forgery-bias-eliminating loss, and conditional-mutual-information regularization. Supplementary material reports FF++ tests, Celeb-DF/DFDC cross-testing and t-SNE feature separation.
observed_reliability_evidence: No direct explanation-validity outcome was observed. The authors report modest AUC/accuracy changes on FF++ and better cross-testing AUC on Celeb-DF/DFDC; t-SNE is used to illustrate separation of Zn/Zp. These support the proposed detector's feature-decomposition/robustness claims only.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The work is about causal feature decomposition for a more interpretable/trustworthy forgery detector, not a direct evaluation of a produced explanation's truth or faithfulness. The reported evidence is accuracy/AUC, cross-domain performance, ablation and t-SNE; no independently verified forensic-region ground truth, attribution randomization/deletion-insertion test, explanation-human rating, or user reliance study was found in the two-page letter or supplement. paper: Explainability-driven adversarial robustness assessment for generalized deepfake detectors
verified_identity: Lorenzo Cirillo, Andrea Gervasio, Irene Amerini; EURASIP Journal on Information Security (2025); DOI 10.1186/s13635-025-00211-9

paper: XPlainVerse: A Million-Scale Benchmark for Explainable Deepfake Detection
verified_identity: Abhijeet Narang, Kartik Kuckreja, Shreya Ghosh, Muhammad Haris Khan, Jianfei Cai, and Abhinav Dhall; arXiv:2607.03562v1, submitted 3 July 2026; 50-page preprint.
relevance_class: 直接强相关：图像深伪解释基准、实体/视觉证据接地指标及解释人评
scope_and_methods: Full-text review of official arXiv v1 (50 PDF pages), including the main paper and appendices on the dataset, human reference annotation, seven-stage human evaluation, metric implementation, limitations, and all 70 numbered references. The benchmark contains about one million images (470K authentic from five sources and 530K manipulated/generated images from twelve editing or synthesis systems); Edit-Check filtering retains about 265K of roughly 609K initial fake candidates. It provides complex and simple explanations and approximately 1.53M explanation records. Twelve annotators wrote complex explanations for 2,000 manipulated images using paired original/edited images. The overlap check uses only ten examples independently annotated by five annotators. Ten adult participants recruited through the authors' institutional research groups took part in the seven-stage human evaluation; the appendix reports stage-specific stimulus/rating counts.
observed_reliability_evidence: Direct, multi-faceted explanation-quality evidence: human ratings report complex explanations at 3.79/5 composite, grounding 3.82, specificity 3.96, completeness 3.78, convincingness 3.79, and unsupported claims 2.43 (lower is better); simple explanations score 3.94/5 with ease 4.11. The authors report overlap-set inter-annotator agreement of EntityScore 0.50 and EvidenceScore 0.44. Their metrics explicitly score diagnostic entity and visual-evidence coverage in addition to BERTScore, addressing content omitted by surface similarity.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The reported overlap agreement is based on ten images and five annotators and is operationalized with the paper's own EntityScore/EvidenceScore semantic-coverage metrics, using the same offline Qwen3.5-4B model for structured extraction and directional coverage judgments; it is not a chance-corrected coefficient such as Cohen/Fleiss kappa or Krippendorff alpha. The metrics compare explanation text to human reference text, not claims independently adjudicated against image pixels or forensic ground truth; reference errors and judge errors can therefore propagate. The human study measures perceived grounding, specificity, completeness, convincingness, unsupported claims, readability, preference, and stated usefulness, not detector-assisted decision accuracy, calibrated trust, or appropriate reliance. The paper does not establish model-decision causal faithfulness, necessity/sufficiency, or perturbation/sanity-check validity. Ten institutionally recruited adults and a geographically concentrated annotation pool limit generalization. OOD grounding drops more than text similarity in the paper's narrative, but the extracted PDF table has font-encoding issues, so no uncertain table values are transcribed here. The paper is arXiv v1; only that version was reviewed. All 70 references received title/topic screening, not 70 cited-work full-text reviews.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a high-priority direct benchmark for explanation grounding and human-rated explanation quality. The full text strengthens the evidence beyond the abstract: it specifies a small overlap-based agreement study, subjective explanation-quality ratings, and a Qwen-judged reference-grounding metric. These establish relevant evaluation procedures but do not establish independent visual factuality, causal faithfulness, or appropriate reliance.

paper: Effect of AI Performance, Risk Perception, and Trust on Human Dependence in Deepfake Detection AI System
verified_identity: Yingfan Zhou, Ester Chen, Manasa Pisipati, Aiping Xiong, Sarah Rajtmajer; Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction 9(7), article CSCW407 (2025), published 2025-10-16; DOI 10.1145/3757588. arXiv:2508.01906v1 title variant: ‘Perceived Risk’; official arXiv v1 submitted 2025-08-03.
relevance_class: Human-reliance / appropriate-reliance neighbor in image deepfake detection; not an explanation-quality experiment
scope_and_methods: Read the complete official arXiv v1 HTML main text (Sections 1–7), references and Appendices A–F; reused the prior 59-position bibliography screen rather than screening it again. Online experiment: 400 recruited, 390 valid U.S. Prolific participants; 32 face images from Nightingale & Farid (2022) shown with outputs from two notional AI systems. The systems were described as having FPR 30% vs 3%; the study had no actual detector and the 32-item prediction sets were deliberately not calibrated to those rates: within each demographic subgroup, each system had one TP, TN, FP and FN. Appendix C further illustrates the high-FPR system by saying 30 of 100 AI-flagged images were actually real, which uses the proportion of flagged images that are false positives rather than the standard FPR denominator (real images).
observed_reliability_evidence: Relevant behavioral evidence: users’ decisions varied with the AI label and the communicated performance profile; the reported risk-group × FPR × AI-prediction interaction was significant (F(1,388)=21.36, p<.001, partial eta-squared=.05). Participants more often followed high-FPR synthetic warnings in the assigned high-risk group (0.63 vs 0.57), while no reliable high/low-FPR difference appeared for AI-real predictions in that group. Trust scale alpha=.89 and risk scale alpha=.84 concern questionnaire internal consistency only. Trust difference was small (3.62 vs 3.75 on a 7-point scale; d=.09), and trust/risk moderated mediation paths were not significant.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: No visual saliency, localized forensic evidence, natural-language rationale, or other model explanation was shown or manipulated; participants saw AI labels and performance information. Therefore this is not empirical evidence about explanation factuality, grounding, faithfulness, stability, or whether explanations improve reliance. The advertised FPR was not reflected in actual item-level errors, and Appendix C's numeric example appears to switch to false-discovery proportion; both weaken interpreting the behavior as calibrated reliance on measured detector reliability. The authors' compliance/reliance ratios use totals conditioned on AI-predicted classes, so they should not be read as a standalone measure of whether humans accept correct versus incorrect AI advice. The assigned risk treatment failed its manipulation check (high-risk M=4.78, low-risk M=4.90, nonsignificant); sample is U.S.-only and recruited from Prolific. All 59 cited positions were already screened in the prior bibliography route and were not repeated here.
screening_conclusion: Keep as a domain-specific human reliance neighbor that motivates appropriate-reliance outcomes for forensic explanation studies. Do not rank it as direct explanation-reliability evidence: no explanation was evaluated. paper: Seeing Before Reasoning: A Unified Framework for Generalizable and Explainable Fake Image Detection
